name: Crawl Hunt – Advanced SEO Optimization Tool
author: themeshopy

sections.description:
Crawl Hunt is a comprehensive WordPress plugin that helps you monitor and track website changes through automated crawling. Perfect for SEO monitoring, content tracking, and staying updated with your website’s status.

This plugin connects to the Crawl Hunt service. You must opt in by clicking “Connect Crawl Hunt” inside the plugin before any data is sent to the service.

Features:

  • Automated website crawling
  • Track URL status and changes
  • REST API integration for external crawlers
  • Simple and intuitive admin interface
  • Detailed crawl logs and history
  • Secure account connection to Crawl Hunt
  • Lightweight and performant

External Service: Crawl Hunt

Data sent to the service:

  • WordPress site URL during connection
  • Account authentication token for API access
  • Dashboard data requests initiated by the user

Terms of Use: https://www.crawlhunt.com/terms-and-conditions
Privacy Policy: https://www.crawlhunt.com/privacy-policy
sections.installation:
1. Go to Plugins > Add New in your WordPress admin panel and search for “Crawl Hunt”, or upload the plugin ZIP file via Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Click Install Now and then Activate the plugin.
  3. A new Crawl Hunt menu item will appear in your WordPress sidebar — click it to open the plugin home screen.
  4. Click the Connect button. A popup will open taking you to the Crawl Hunt website. If you do not have an account, create a free one at https://www.crawlhunt.com.
  5. Sign in to your Crawl Hunt account. The popup will close automatically and your WordPress site will be connected.
  6. Return to the Crawl Hunt plugin in WordPress — the status banner will now show Connected.
  7. Click Open Crawl Hunt Application to open the Crawl Hunt dashboard in a new tab.
  8. In the Crawl Hunt dashboard, go to Projects and click Run Audit to start your first SEO crawl of your WordPress site.
  9. Once the crawl completes, navigate to the Issues tab to review all detected SEO problems grouped by type and priority.
  10. Use the AI Fix or Edit actions on each issue to apply changes — updates are written back to your WordPress site automatically through the plugin.
sections.faq:
Do I need to connect my Crawl Hunt account?

Yes. Click “Connect” in the plugin interface to authorize the plugin to access your account.

How do I integrate with external crawlers?

You can use the REST API endpoint at /wp-json/crawl-hunt/v1/log to send crawl data. Include your API key in the X-API-Key header if configured.

Does this plugin load external code?

No. All scripts and styles are bundled with the plugin. The external Crawl Hunt service is contacted only after you connect your account.
sections.changelog:
1.0.10

  • Added: New Theme Fix — “Disallow Files” lets you block selected file types (e.g. feeds) from being crawled by adding matching Disallow rules to your site’s live robots.txt.
  • Added: New Theme Fix — Blog Image Dimensions scans published posts for <img> tags missing explicit width/height, and can apply fixes in bulk to reduce Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS), with the ability to revert to the original content.
  • Added: IndexNow key file hosting — the plugin can now write and remove the IndexNow verification key file at your site root as part of the IndexNow integration.
  • Improved: Enqueued stylesheets are now actually rewritten into non-blocking preload tags (with a <noscript> fallback) instead of being left untouched — previously this filter was a compliance-only no-op.
  • Improved: Dashboard and Home page redesigned with a refreshed visual style, including a personalized “Good morning, {site name}” welcome greeting.

1.0.9

  • Improved: Dashboard primary stats (SEO Score, Total Pages, Pages with Issues, Broken Links) now animate with a count-up effect when the page loads.
  • Improved: Core Web Vitals bars and metric tiles are now color-coded green / amber / red using official Google thresholds (LCP, FCP, TBT, CLS).
  • Improved: Thematic Reports cards (Crawlability, HTTPS, Accessibility) now display inline SVG icons above each badge for faster visual scanning.
  • Improved: Errors and Warnings section redesigned as metric cards with a colored icon badge, large value, title, and description — replacing the plain number layout.
  • Improved: HTTPS Coverage and Mobile-Friendly stat cards now include a progress bar below the value for at-a-glance coverage visibility.
  • Improved: All five Lighthouse score cards (Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, SEO, PWA) now display a tooltip on hover explaining what each score measures.
  • Improved: Hover lift animation unified across Dashboard and Home — both now use translateY(-1px).
  • Improved: Stat value font sizes normalized — metric-container values reduced from 48 px to 36 px to match the primary stats grid.
  • Improved: Status badge colours (2xx / 3xx / 4xx) now match the exact palette used by the Pages by Status Code bar chart.
  • Improved: Responsive breakpoints standardised — Pages by Status Code chart, Lighthouse metrics grid, and Thematic Reports grid all now collapse at 1024 px instead of 900 px.
  • Improved: Empty state padding increased from 28 px to 32 px across all dashboard sections for better visual breathing room.

1.0.8

  • Improved: Connection status banner now displays a pulsing ring animation on the connected indicator dot and applies a green-tinted background with matching border when the site is connected.
  • Improved: Home page hero section redesigned with a blue gradient background, animated feature icons, staggered card animations on load, a highlighted final-CTA box, and an animated arrow on CTA buttons.
  • Improved: Dashboard stats grid now shows colored left-border accents per stat, alternating table row striping with hover highlight, and Lighthouse score cards color-coded by performance tier.
  • Improved: Dashboard loading state replaced with a shimmer skeleton layout matching the page structure.
  • Improved: All four empty-state messages in the dashboard upgraded with centered layout, inline SVG icons, and improved typography.

1.0.7

  • Fixed: Bulk AI Fix no longer fails with “Page not found for URL” for taxonomy archive pages (WooCommerce product categories, product tags, and any other public custom taxonomy). The plugin now correctly resolves these URLs and applies SEO meta updates via Yoast SEO and Rank Math.
  • Improved: Error messages for URLs that cannot be resolved now explain specifically why the fix could not be applied — covering cases such as a different domain, date archives, author archives, search results pages, and deleted or renamed pages — instead of showing the generic “Page not found for URL” error.

1.0.6

  • Added: Plugin now redirects to the Crawl Hunt home screen automatically after activation.
  • Added: Product tour for first-time users — guides through the Connect button, Open App button, How It Works section, and the final CTA. Accessible at any time via the “Take a tour” link.
  • Improved: Connect flow redesigned to match the Shopify integration. Clicking Connect now registers the site with Crawl Hunt, creates or links the user account using the WordPress admin email, and opens a short-lived login link in a popup — no pre-existing crawlhunt.com session required.
  • Improved: Popup closes automatically after a successful connection and the status banner refreshes in place without a page reload.
  • Improved: “Open Crawl Hunt Application” button now reads “Start Free SEO Scan” when the site is not yet connected.
  • Fixed: Tour popover font rendering — added explicit font-smoothing and font-family declarations to counteract driver.js all: unset reset.
  • Fixed: Tour popover was rendering as a small invisible dot because driver.js CSS was not being extracted by wp-scripts. Base styles are now enqueued as a standalone stylesheet.

1.0.5

  • Fixed: readme.txt external service links now render as proper anchors on WordPress.org.
  • Fixed: Data sent to service list now renders as proper unordered list on WordPress.org.
  • Improved: Expanded installation instructions with a full 10-step guide covering connection, audit, and fix workflow.

1.0.4

  • Fixed: Replaced manual canonical and schema tag output paths with WordPress built-in canonical/script APIs.
  • Fixed: Updated asset loading and path handling for WordPress.org compliance.

1.0.3

  • Fixed: Removed Shopify references from the plugin settings page to comply with WordPress.org guidelines.
  • Fixed: Removed all locked or restricted built-in features to comply with Guideline 5 (no trialware or feature gating).

1.0.2

  • Fixed: Replaced raw inline script output with wp_print_inline_script_tag() in auth.php
  • Fixed: Debug log paths now use wp_upload_dir() and WP_CONTENT_DIR instead of hardcoded ABSPATH references
  • Fixed: Renamed JavaScript global crawlHuntConfig to crawlHuntSEOAudit for uniqueness

1.0.1

  • Fixed: Resolved WordPress database query warnings in auth.php
  • Improved: Optimized meta query for OAuth state validation

1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • Basic crawling log functionality
  • Admin dashboard and settings
  • REST API integration
